$comment: The open-core boundary (S27). Single source of truth for which paths belong to the
public upstream and which stay private. Consumed by scripts/check-straddle.mjs (the
pre-commit hook and CI) and, from S27 P1, by the history audit and materialisation.
EP1: this is configuration, not a constant buried in a script. Adding a top-level
directory means editing THIS file, not three call sites.
Why `specs/` is PUBLIC while `.kiro/` is PRIVATE, which looks inconsistent and is not:
they are two different sprint queues for two different scopes. `.kiro/specs/appbay-v1/`
is the private product's queue (the web UI, the desktop app, the journeys) and stays
private. `specs/` is the CLI's own queue — sprints whose work is entirely public-set, so
the sprint record must travel upstream with the code it governs. A CLI sprint recorded
only in the private tree would be invisible to the repo that actually holds the code.
Why it matters that a commit never touches both sets: the private repo is a fork of
the public one, and public-set commits are sent upstream by cherry-pick. A commit
spanning both cannot be cherry-picked without dragging private files with it.
Measured over the 100 commits before 2026-08-15: 16 public-only, 51 private-only, 11
straddling — and seven of those eleven were a code fix plus its own .kiro record, i.e.
a documentation habit rather than real coupling.
$shared: Files matching neither set are SHARED — root config (package.json, turbo.json,
pnpm-workspace.yaml, tsconfig.json, .gitignore), README.md, Makefile, tests/, and the
journeys under scripts/journeys/. They are exempt because they must stay byte-identical
across both repos; a commit touching only shared files straddles nothing.
pnpm-workspace.yaml is the load-bearing one: it uses globs (packages/*, apps/*), so the
public repo simply has fewer directories matching and the file never needs to differ.
Had it enumerated packages, every merge from upstream would conflict on it forever.
